label: lem:edge-id
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Edge identities

title: Proof
body_md:
The identities~\eqref{eq:phi-prod} follow by expanding $\phi(x)=\sqrt\kappa(e_x-u)$, and~\eqref{eq:phi-cov} follows from $\sum_xe_x=\mathbf{1}$ and $\sum_xe_xe_x^{\intercal}=I$.
	For the sums over pairs, extend $A_{ij}(\boldsymbol{\sigma}):=\phi(\sigma_i)^{\intercal}\phi(\sigma_j)$ to all $i,j$, so that $A_{ii}(\boldsymbol{\sigma})=\kappa-1$.
	Summing~\eqref{eq:phi-prod} over all ordered pairs $(i,j)$ gives
	\begin{align*}
		\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}(\boldsymbol{\sigma})=\left\Vert\textstyle\sum_i\phi(\sigma_i)\right\Vert_2^2=N\left\Vertm(\boldsymbol{\sigma})\right\Vert_2^2,
	\end{align*}
	and in the same way
	\begin{align*}
		\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}(\boldsymbol{\sigma})A_{ij}(\boldsymbol{\tau})
		=\left\Vert\textstyle\sum_i\phi(\sigma_i)\phi(\tau_i)^{\intercal}\right\Vert_F^2
		=N\left\Vert\mathscr{R}(\boldsymbol{\sigma},\boldsymbol{\tau})\right\Vert_F^2.
	\end{align*}
	Subtracting the diagonal contributions $N(\kappa-1)$ and $N(\kappa-1)^2$ and dividing by two proves~\eqref{eq:vertex-edge} and~\eqref{eq:pair-edge}.
	The two possible edge values give $A_{ij}^2=(\kappa-2)A_{ij}+\kappa-1$.
	Summing this identity over $i<j$ and applying~\eqref{eq:vertex-edge} and~\eqref{eq:pair-edge} gives~\eqref{eq:selfoverlap}.

	For the three-replica identity, the inner product of tensor products gives
	\begin{align*}
		N\left\VertR^{(3)}(\boldsymbol{\sigma},\boldsymbol{\tau},\boldsymbol{\tau}')\right\Vert_F^2
		=\sum_{i,j}A_{ij}(\boldsymbol{\sigma})A_{ij}(\boldsymbol{\tau})A_{ij}(\boldsymbol{\tau}').
	\end{align*}
	Subtracting the diagonal contribution $N(\kappa-1)^3$ and dividing by $2N$ proves~\eqref{eq:triple-edge}.
	By exchangeability and~\eqref{eq:vertex-edge}, for $i\ne j$,
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{\mathds{E}}_{\boldsymbol{\sigma}}^{(\boldsymbol{n})}\big(A_{ij}(\boldsymbol{\sigma})\big)
		=\frac{\left\Vertm_{\boldsymbol{n}}\right\Vert_2^2-\kappa+1}{N-1}.
	\end{align*}
	Taking expectations in~\eqref{eq:triple-edge} and using the independence of the three configurations proves~\eqref{eq:triple-overlap-moment}.

label: lem:general-profile-moments
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Mixed second moments and profile comparison

title: Proof
body_md:
By the definitions of $\mathcal{Z}_N$ and $\Lambda_N$,
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\big(\mathcal{Z}_N^{(\boldsymbol{n})}\mathcal{Z}_N^{(\boldsymbol{n}')}\big)
		=\operatorname{\mathds{E}}_{\boldsymbol{\sigma},\boldsymbol{\tau}}^{(\boldsymbol{n}),(\boldsymbol{n}')}\Big(
		\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\big(e_N(\boldsymbol{\sigma})e_N(\boldsymbol{\tau})\big)\Big)
		=\operatorname{\mathds{E}}_{\boldsymbol{\sigma},\boldsymbol{\tau}}^{(\boldsymbol{n}),(\boldsymbol{n}')}\big(e^{\Lambda_N(\boldsymbol{\sigma},\boldsymbol{\tau})}\big).
	\end{align*}
	Choose $\beta^2<s<\alpha_c(\kappa)$. Lemma~\ref{lem:profile-moments}(i), applied with exponent $s$, gives the uniform integrability of $e^{\beta^2\xi(\mathscr{R})}$ over the profile window. By Lemma~\ref{lem:general-kernels}, $\mathfrak{R}_N^{(2)}$ is uniformly bounded and converges to zero in probability, uniformly over the profiles. Hence
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{\mathds{E}}_{\boldsymbol{\sigma},\boldsymbol{\tau}}^{(\boldsymbol{n}),(\boldsymbol{n}')}\Big(
		e^{\beta^2\xi(\mathscr{R})}\,\left\verte^{\mathfrak{R}_N^{(2)}}-1\right\vert\Big)\longrightarrow0
	\end{align*}
	uniformly over the window. Combining~\eqref{eq:general-pair-kernel} with Lemma~\ref{lem:profile-moments}(ii), we obtain
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{\mathds{E}}_{\boldsymbol{\sigma},\boldsymbol{\tau}}^{(\boldsymbol{n}),(\boldsymbol{n}')}\big(e^{\Lambda_N}\big)
		=e^{\varphi_{\kappa,J}(\beta^2)-\varphi_\kappa(\beta^2)}\,
		\operatorname{\mathds{E}}_{\boldsymbol{\sigma},\boldsymbol{\tau}}^{(\boldsymbol{n}),(\boldsymbol{n}')}\big(e^{\beta^2\xi(\mathscr{R})}\big)+o(1)
		\longrightarrow e^{\varphi_{\kappa,J}(\beta^2)},
	\end{align*}
	uniformly over the profiles. This proves~\eqref{eq:general-mixed-second}.

	Finally, $\left\Vertm_{\boldsymbol{n}^*}\right\Vert_2\to0$, so $\boldsymbol{n}^*$ belongs to the window for all large $N$. Expand the square in~\eqref{eq:general-profile-collapse} and apply~\eqref{eq:general-mixed-second} to the profile pairs $(\boldsymbol{n},\boldsymbol{n})$, $(\boldsymbol{n},\boldsymbol{n}^*)$, and $(\boldsymbol{n}^*,\boldsymbol{n}^*)$. All three moments have the same limit, uniformly in $\boldsymbol{n}$, and their coefficients $1,-2,1$ sum to zero.

label: lem:loop-chaos
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Loop moments

title: Proof
body_md:
(i) Two distinct loops have an edge that lies in only one of them. Independence and centering of the edges therefore make their monomials orthogonal, which proves~\eqref{eq:Wcov}. Moreover,
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\big(Y_{N,n}(\mathcal{J}_N)^2\big)=\frac1{N^n}\sum_{\gamma\in\mathcal{L}_n}\prod_{e\in\gamma}\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\big(\mathcal{J}_{N,e}^2\big)
		\longrightarrow\frac1{2n},
	\end{align*}
	since $\left\vert\mathcal{L}_n\right\vert=(N)_n/(2n)$ and the edge variances converge uniformly to $1$.

	(ii) In this proof write $Y:=Y_{N,n}(\mathcal{J}_N)$, $\tau_e:=\mathcal{J}_{N,e}/\sqrt N$, and $\tau^\gamma:=\prod_{e\in\gamma}\tau_e$. Uniform integrability implies $\sup_{N,e}\operatorname{\mathds{E}}(\mathcal{J}_{N,e}^4)<\infty$, so $\operatorname{\mathds{E}}(\left\vert\tau_e\right\vert^p)\leqslant C N^{-p/2}$ for $2\leqslant p\leqslant4$. We expand over quadruples $\boldsymbol{q}=(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_4)\in\mathcal{L}_n^4$:
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{\mathds{E}}(Y^4)-3\,\operatorname{\mathds{E}}(Y^2)^2=\sum_{\boldsymbol{q}\in\mathcal{L}_n^4}\mathcal{K}(\boldsymbol{q}),\quad
		\mathcal{K}(\boldsymbol{q}):=\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\Big(\prod_{i=1}^4\tau^{\gamma_i}\Big)
		-\sum_{\{\{i,j\},\{k,l\}\}}\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\big(\tau^{\gamma_i}\tau^{\gamma_j}\big)\,\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\big(\tau^{\gamma_k}\tau^{\gamma_l}\big),
	\end{align*}
	where the inner sum runs over the three pairings of $[4]$.
	Let $\Gamma := \gamma_1 \cup \cdots \cup \gamma_4$, and let $\nu_e$ be the number of loops $\gamma_i$ that contain $e$. Then $\sum_{e \in \Gamma} \nu_e = 4n$ and $1 \leqslant \nu_e \leqslant 4$. By independence, $\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\big(\prod_i \tau^{\gamma_i}\big) = \prod_{e \in \Gamma}\operatorname{\mathds{E}}(\tau_e^{\nu_e})$. If some $\nu_e=1$, the joint expectation vanishes. Each pairing term vanishes as well, since a nonzero pairing term requires two pairs of identical loops, and then every edge has even multiplicity. Hence $\mathcal{K}(\boldsymbol{q}) = 0$ unless $\nu_e \geqslant 2$ for all $e$. In that case the joint term and each nonzero pairing term are bounded in absolute value by
	\begin{align*}
		\prod_{e \in \Gamma} C N^{-\nu_e/2} = C^{\left\vert\Gamma\right\vert} N^{-2n} \leqslant C(n) N^{-2n},
	\end{align*}
	so $\left\vert\mathcal{K}(\boldsymbol{q})\right\vert \leqslant C(n)N^{-2n}$. Since $\nu_e \geqslant 2$ for all $e$, we have $\left\vert\Gamma\right\vert \leqslant 2n$. Moreover, $\Gamma$ is a union of cycles, so every vertex of $\Gamma$ has degree at least $2$. Hence $\left\vertV(\Gamma)\right\vert \leqslant \left\vert\Gamma\right\vert \leqslant 2n$, with equality in the first inequality exactly when $\Gamma$ is a vertex-disjoint union of cycles.

	Suppose that $\left\vertV(\Gamma)\right\vert = 2n$. Then $\left\vert\Gamma\right\vert = 2n$, hence $\nu_e=2$ for every $e\in\Gamma$, and $\Gamma$ is a vertex-disjoint union of cycles. Each $\gamma_i$ is then a whole component of $\Gamma$. So every component of $\Gamma$ is one of the $\gamma_i$ and has length $n$, and $\left\vert\Gamma\right\vert = 2n$ leaves exactly two components. In other words, $\boldsymbol{q}$ consists of two vertex-disjoint loops $\gamma \neq \gamma'$, each occurring twice. For such $\boldsymbol{q}$ the joint term is $\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\big((\tau^{\gamma})^2\big) \operatorname{\mathds{E}}\big((\tau^{\gamma'})^2\big)$. Exactly one of the three pairings matches the two equal pairs and contributes the same value, and the other two vanish. Hence $\mathcal{K}(\boldsymbol{q}) = 0$.

	Only quadruples with $\left\vertV(\Gamma)\right\vert \leqslant 2n-1$ therefore contribute. The number of quadruples with a prescribed isomorphism type of $(\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_4)$ is at most $C(n)N^{\left\vertV(\Gamma)\right\vert}$, and the number of types is bounded in terms of $n$. So these quadruples contribute at most $C(n)N^{2n-1}\cdot C(n)N^{-2n} = C(n)/N$, which proves (ii).

	(iii) The normalized loop monomials $N^{-n/2}\prod_{e\in\gamma}\mathcal{J}_{N,e}$ are Hoeffding components of order $n$. A fixed edge belongs to $\mathcal{O}(N^{n-2})$ loops, each with variance $\mathcal{O}(N^{-n})$, so its influence is $\mathcal{O}(N^{-2})$. Since the variances have positive limits, this bound persists after normalization.

label: lem:quadratic-moments
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Quadratic moments

title: Proof
body_md:
Independence gives $\operatorname{Var}\big(X_N(\mathcal{J}_N)\big)=N^{-2}\sum_e\operatorname{Var}(\mathcal{J}_{N,e}^2)\to v$. The cutoff error is $N^{-1}$ times the centered sum of the independent variables $\mathcal{J}_{N,e}^2\mathds{1}\{\left\vert\mathcal{J}_{N,e}\right\vert\geqslant M\}$, which gives~\eqref{eq:quadratic-truncation-error}.

	Write $Q_e:=(\mathcal{J}_{N,e}^{(M)})^2-\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\big((\mathcal{J}_{N,e}^{(M)})^2\big)$. The uniform fourth-moment bound gives $\operatorname{\mathds{E}}(Q_e^2)\leqslant C$ and
	$\operatorname{\mathds{E}}(Q_e^4)\leqslant16\,\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\big((\mathcal{J}_{N,e}^{(M)})^8\big)\leqslant CM^4$. By independence and centering,
	\begin{align*}
		\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\big(X_N^{(M)}(\mathcal{J}_N)^4\big)-3\operatorname{Var}\big(X_N^{(M)}(\mathcal{J}_N)\big)^2
		&=\frac1{N^4}\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\Big(\Big(\sum_e Q_e\Big)^4\Big)-\frac3{N^4}\,\operatorname{\mathds{E}}\Big(\Big(\sum_e Q_e\Big)^2\Big)^2\\
		&=\frac1{N^4}\sum_e\Big(\operatorname{\mathds{E}}(Q_e^4)-3\,\operatorname{\mathds{E}}(Q_e^2)^2\Big)
		=\mathcal{O}(M^4N^{-2}).
	\end{align*}
	Each $Q_e/N$ is a Hoeffding component of order $1$ with variance at most $C/N^2$, which proves the influence bound.

title: Proof
body_md:
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:balanced_clt} to $\boldsymbol{n}^*(N)$ and add~\eqref{eq:transfer-full}.
	The profile cardinalities cancel, and $\left\Vertm_{\boldsymbol{n}^*}\right\Vert_2^2\to0$.
	Passing to the centering of the statement subtracts
	$\beta^2(\kappa-1)(\kappa-2)/4=(\kappa-1)\alpha/2$.
	Since
	\begin{align*}
		-\frac{\kappa-1}{2}\alpha
		-\frac{\kappa-1}{2}\ln(1-\alpha)
		=(\kappa-1)\varphi(\alpha),
	\end{align*}
	the stated formula follows.
